doc: Machine-readable engineering policy catalogue. level: MANDATORY (a violation blocks), RECOMMENDED (pattern; deviate with a note), EXCEPTION_ADR (allowed only with an ADR). enforcement.kind: executable (a script/test fails on violation), hook (blocked at tool time), review (human/agent review step) or manual (no automation yet, reason required). Tested by scripts/governance.test.mjs.

policies.statement: Every controller is classified (standard-mutable | read-only | action | sensitive) in api-resource-contracts.json.
A standard-mutable resource declares create/get/list/update/delete, or records why one is not applicable.
Read-only and sensitive resources expose no destructive verb without an explicit, justified allow entry.
Every non-@Public route is behind @UseGuards.

Every route has a supported authorization contract (permission decorators, platform permission/role guard, machine-token guard, @AuthenticationOnly, @Public, rate-limited public); a legacy gap must sit in the authorization register with a priority, an owner role and a due date, and the gate fails when the date passes.
Unknown request fields are a 400 (whitelist + forbidNonWhitelisted); DTO and frontend payload change together.
A breaking change to a public API response, permission key, enum value or settings key needs an approved transition.

enforcement.reason: no OpenAPI baseline is committed yet; see roadmap item R-1 in docs/engineering/automation-matrix.md

policies.statement: Tenant-owned queries filter on tenantId from request.user, never from client input.
Responses and import/export templates never expose password hashes, tokens, encrypted secrets or internal columns.
No secret is committed; new env vars are registered in config validation, render.yaml and docs.
Production advisories are resolved or argued in a record; the allowlist is never widened to go green.
Every code path that writes a CustomizationTable is registered with a reason.
Custom-module creation provisions the full component plan inside one transaction and is reconcilable.
The component plan has unique keys, one default form and one default view, and no view whose filter the runtime would drop.
Provisioning is idempotent and never rewrites or renames an existing customisation.
Never run migrate reset or db push against a shared database; never hand-edit an applied migration.
A destructive schema change needs an ExecPlan with backfill and rollback; use expand/backfill/contract.
Required configuration rows are added to seed-config and verified by verify-seed-config.
No agent pushes or merges to main; ordinary work integrates into develop.
Never force-push; never discard an unverified commit.
Never undo work with checkout --, restore, reset --hard or clean in a shared tree.
Remove worktrees only through the guarded script (junction-safe).
A CI failure is classified by cause before it is acted on; the first failure's evidence is preserved.
Only verified-transient infrastructure causes are retryable; a failing test is never retried into green.
Hooks and signing are never bypassed to obtain a green build.
Required checks and warning budgets are never loosened to go green; CI policy changes need review.
Run the fast preflight (npm run preflight) before every push.
Only P0/P1 incidents use the emergency path; P2/P3 follow the normal flow unless the owner escalates.
A hotfix baseline is the verified deployed SHA, never an assumption that it equals origin/main.
A hotfix may narrow scope but never drops lint, build or the authorization regression.
A migration in a hotfix must be expand-only; destructive changes are refused.
Production deployment of a hotfix requires explicit owner approval; tooling cannot grant it.
A deployed hotfix is backported to develop and its incident record closed.

enforcement.reason: backport is a post-deploy human/agent step; a reminder is in the runbook but no gate can observe it

policies.statement: The owner decides pricing/entitlements, material business rules, destructive data changes, security weakening, breaking public API changes, production deployment and new recurring cost; agents never invent a business requirement to avoid asking.
An implementation agent never declares its own change independently QA-approved.
Skills and agents are valid, versioned in Git and registered; rules are not duplicated across files.
A lesson becomes a rule only through a reviewed commit; no agent edits its own policy silently.
Use the shared table/form/empty-state components; every data surface has loading, error and empty states.
Do not add explanatory helper copy to controls without asking the owner.
Index every foreign key and (tenantId, filter column) pair a list screen sorts or filters by; avoid N+1 queries and duplicate frontend requests.
A material decision is an ADR; a recurring operation is a runbook; every control states whether it is automated.
Authorization classification is evidence-based: the route-level inventory traces handler to service and names what it found; a classification can be disproved from the inventory.
Package import gives the modules it creates their missing defaults, create-only, never overwriting imported definitions.

What a module is provisioned with depends on its kind: My Records only where users own records, Active/Inactive only where records can be deactivated, no edit/delete/deactivate commands where the lifecycle forbids them.

Reconciliation of existing modules is explicit and tenant-scoped: dry run by default, apply needs the retyped workspace slug plus an owner authorization reference on production, and it is never wired to startup, seeding or a schedule.
The record lifecycle is enforced by the API by module kind (immutable records are never changed; configuration records are never deleted) and the UI capabilities are derived from the same rules.
Every CI job installs through the shared setup action, which pins the npm declared in package.json and verifies node and npm before any dependency install.
Dependabot targets develop (never production), has a single npm entry at the repository root so one bump opens one pull request, and groups routine updates.

The emergency path is rehearsed end to end against a throwaway repository and a fake production target, stopping at the approval checkpoint unless explicitly simulated, and the rehearsal can never touch the real repository.
Finishing a session closes its durable record and regenerates the indexes in one step; a session cannot be left ACTIVE by a finished task.
Counts a script can compute (models, enums, migrations, public handlers, modules) are derived into the instruction files, not typed, and checked on every push.
